study.title: Aleniglipron, a daily oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist, in adults with obesity: a phase 2b randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial

cover.headline: Take the needle out of obesity medicine and **far more people can actually start.**

slides.title: A daily pill skips the cold chain, the prescriber training and the fear of needles.
slides.body:
Semaglutide and tirzepatide changed obesity medicine and both arrive as a weekly injection. That is a hard no for a large share of the people they would help.

An oral version is the same receptor with the barrier removed.

slides.title: Across 38 US sites, the top dose beat placebo by roughly twelve percentage points.
slides.body:
230 adults were split at random between three doses and a placebo for 36 weeks. The top dose took off 12.1% of body weight; placebo managed 0.5%.

One in ten stopped early. Gut side effects eased over time.

stat.label: body weight lost on the top dose

slides.title: The peptide drugs fall apart in the gut, which is why this one is not a peptide.
slides.body:
Chemists went looking for a small molecule that hits the GLP-1 receptor and survives being swallowed. Aleniglipron is one of those.

This is the phase 2b readout: it works, at a dose people mostly tolerated.

caveats: The trial was funded by Structure Therapeutics, the company that owns the drug.
Phase 2b means 230 people over 36 weeks. Rare harms only show up in far larger trials.
Around one in ten quit before the end, so tolerability is not a solved problem.
Weight regain after stopping was not tested here. For every other GLP-1, it happens.

cta.headline: Send this to whoever says weight-loss pills need needles
cta.sub: One real study, every weekday. The full paper is linked in bio.

caption: The interesting number is not the 12.1% lost. It is that you swallow this one, and 0.5% is what placebo managed.
